items.text: Claude GitHub App installed on ck5o4/multifamily with write access - cloud push unblocked
items.why: FIXED 2026-08-17 by Anthony. Root cause was subtler than 'a missing scope': the Claude app was AUTHORIZED on ck5o4 but INSTALLED only on the flux-brain-hq org, never on the personal account that owns multifamily. Authorization is what let cloud sessions read; installation is what grants repo Contents:write, so every push 403'd while every read succeeded - exactly the observed asymmetry. Installed via github.com/apps/claude/installations/new -> ck5o4 -> Only select repositories -> multifamily. Verified at installation 154488689: 'Read and write access to ... code' and 'Selected 1 repository: ck5o4/multifamily'. Scoped to that one repo deliberately. NOTE: the post-install redirect lands on claude.ai/admin-settings/... which shows 'You don't have access to organization settings' on a personal plan - that dead end is cosmetic, not a failure. CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 PM: the scheduled cloud sweep pushed to origin/main for real (3254356..feb4e3a). No 403, no recovery-patch email. TRAP FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: the cloud container starts on a DETACHED HEAD with the local 'main' ref left at a stale commit, so 'git push -u origin main' fails with 'behind its remote' and reads exactly like the old permissions failure. It is not. Fix is 'git branch -f main HEAD && git checkout main' before pushing, or push HEAD:main. SECOND HALF OF THE TRAP, found 2026-08-18: the stale ref is not just local 'main' - the remote-tracking ref 'origin/main' is ALSO stale on container start. This run opened with 'git log origin/main..HEAD' listing 9 commits that looked unpushed (including work already confirmed pushed on 08-18 PM). They were not unpushed; the container's cached origin/main simply predated them. A single 'git fetch origin main' moved origin/main ccdf19f..f38b13b and the list went empty. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUTINE: step 4 tells the scan to judge the git-push-rule todo by whether 'git log origin/main..HEAD' is empty, so ALWAYS fetch before running that test - otherwise a clean repo reads as 9 commits of lost work and the scan will 'recover' work that was never lost.

items.text: Pin openpyxl in the environment setup for scheduled cloud runs
items.why: openpyxl is absent in every fresh cloud container. Without it tools/board.py replaces BOTH live deal cards (Eden, Treme) with 'could not compute' placeholders and the board drops from ~17KB to ~10.8KB; it does print ERRORS, so it is not silent. requirements.txt was written into a container working tree 2026-08-15 but could not reach the repo because of the push 403, so it recurs every run. CREATED FOR REAL in the repo by the local session 2026-08-17 - this closes once the cloud setup step installs from it. Local machine is unaffected (openpyxl 3.1.5 present). RECURRED 2026-08-18 scan: absent again in the fresh container, and it blocks MORE than the board - tools/test_pymodel.py imports openpyxl at line 19 and died on import, so the health step could not run at all until it was installed. WORKAROUND CONFIRMED THIS RUN: 'pip install -r requirements.txt' succeeds inside the container (pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org are on the proxy noProxy bypass list, so PyPI is reachable even though FRED is not). After installing, all three suites ran and the board rendered full-size at 24,987 bytes. So the fix is purely to add that one install line to the cloud setup step; nothing in the repo needs to change. RECURRED AGAIN 2026-08-19 (third consecutive cloud scan: 08-17, 08-18, 08-19). Same signature: tools/test_pymodel.py and tools/test_regressions.py both died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' before running a single assertion; tools/test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it again in ~10 seconds, after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 27,359 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Nothing in the repo needs changing - requirements.txt is correct and committed. The one-line fix remains: add 'pip install -r requirements.txt' to the cloud environment setup step. RECURRED A FOURTH TIME 2026-08-20 (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20). Identical signature: test_pymodel.py died at openpyxl import line 19, test_regressions.py died at pymodel._load_deal openpyxl import; test_mc.py passed. 'pip3 install -q -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds, then all three suites passed and board.py rendered 29,307 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Still the same one-line setup fix. RECURRED A FIFTH TIME 2026-08-21 (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20, 08-21). Identical signature: tools/test_pymodel.py died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' (import line 19) before a single assertion ran; test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds (openpyxl 3.1.5 + et-xmlfile 2.0.0), after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 30,721 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Five consecutive scans, same one-line setup fix, nothing in the repo needs changing. RECURRED 2026-08-22: absent again in the fresh container — tools/test_pymodel.py died at the line-19 import before any test ran. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in-container again and the board then wrote 32,819 bytes (full cards, not the ~10.8KB degraded fallback). Five straight runs now start with this manual step; the cloud setup step still does not install from requirements.txt. RECURRED A SEVENTH TIME 2026-08-23 (08-17 through 08-23, every consecutive cloud scan). Identical signature: tools/test_pymodel.py died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' (import line 19) and tools/test_regressions.py died at the same import inside pymodel._load_deal, both before a single assertion ran; test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds (openpyxl 3.1.5 + et-xmlfile 2.0.0), after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 33,993 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Nothing in the repo needs changing; the one-line fix is still to add 'pip install -r requirements.txt' to the cloud environment setup step. | DONE 2026-08-24: SessionStart hook installs requirements.txt on remote runs (.claude/hooks/session-start.sh).

items.text: Allow fred.stlouisfed.org and the comp websites in the CLOUD environment network policy
items.why: CLOUD-ONLY - scoped correctly 2026-08-17. In cloud containers the egress proxy returns 403 CONNECT for fred.stlouisfed.org (killing tools/rates.py with 'curl exit 56') and for parcatdenhamsprings.com and springtreedenham.com (killing the marketwatch snapshot). Both ran CLEAN from the local machine on 2026-08-17 - rates: WSJ Prime 6.75 pct, 10yr 4.68 pct, SOFR 3.62 pct, no drift vs defaults.py; marketwatch: snapshot 2026-08-17 saved, all four properties OK. So the scan is not broken, it is only broken unattended. Until the policy is fixed, rates and marketwatch must be run locally. HARD EVIDENCE 2026-08-18: the proxy's own status endpoint now names the failure explicitly - curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status reports recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443'. Both FRED hostnames are blocked (fred.stlouisfed.org AND api.stlouisfed.org), each returning 'curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. IMPORTANT NUANCE: do NOT read 'the container has no network' - PyPI installs work fine because pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org sit on the proxy noProxy bypass list. This is a per-host allowlist, so the fix is to add fred.stlouisfed.org, api.stlouisfed.org, parcatdenhamsprings.com and springtreedenham.com to the ENVIRONMENT's network policy (the environment was created with a restricted egress policy; see code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). Rates have now gone unverified in cloud on 08-17 and 08-18 - the 6.75 pct Prime in defaults.py is carried from the 08-17 LOCAL run, not confirmed today. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-19, still blocked, now THREE consecutive cloud scans without verified rates (08-17, 08-18, 08-19). tools/rates.py died identically at 'FRED unreachable for DPRIME: curl exit 56'; the proxy status endpoint again logged recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443' (two entries, 2026-08-19T14:15Z). Per /root/.ccr/README.md a 403 from the proxy is an org egress-policy denial that must be reported, not retried or routed around, so this run did not attempt a workaround. CONSEQUENCE: the 6.75 pct WSJ Prime in defaults.py has now been carried unverified for 2 days beyond its 2026-08-17 local confirmation. It is not known to be wrong - it is simply unchecked. Verify locally before pricing any deal. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-20, still blocked, now FOUR consecutive cloud scans without verified rates (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20). tools/rates.py died at 'FRED unreachable for DPRIME: curl exit 56'; direct curl to fred.stlouisfed.org returned 'curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'; the proxy status endpoint logged recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443' (2026-08-20T14:14Z). Per /root/.ccr/README.md a 403 is an org egress-policy denial - reported, not routed around. The 6.75 pct WSJ Prime in defaults.py is now carried unverified for 3 days past its 2026-08-17 local confirmation. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-21, still blocked, now FIVE consecutive cloud scans without verified rates (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20, 08-21). tools/rates.py died at 'FRED unreachable for DPRIME: curl exit 56'; direct curl to fred.stlouisfed.org returned 'curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'; the proxy status endpoint logged recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443' (2026-08-21T14:13:51Z). Per /root/.ccr/README.md a 403 is an org egress-policy denial - reported, not routed around. The 6.75 pct WSJ Prime in defaults.py is now carried unverified for 4 days past its 2026-08-17 local confirmation. items.text: St. Bernard Parish is IN the buy box - resolved by modelling, not by rule
items.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-17 by running the same 12-unit building through three parishes instead of arguing from millage. Price that clears 13%: Baker $528K (equity $146,520), Gretna $397K (equity $110,168), Chalmette $388K (equity $107,670). Chalmette vs Gretna is a $9,000 / 2.3% difference - noise. St. Bernard's heavier millage is NOT what moves the number. The $140K / 26.5% gap vs Baker is the METRO WIND INSURANCE ($3,000/unit vs $2,000), which hits Jefferson and Orleans identically. Conclusion: excluding St. Bernard while buying Gretna is incoherent - same deal, 2.3% apart. All three fit inside $300K capital comfortably, so capital is not the binding constraint on metro deals; the insurance quote is. Chalmette listing itself is Zone X shaded, NOT SFHA, so no lender-required flood policy - but that is post-Katrina levee protection, not natural safety, so price a voluntary policy.
